facts.text: In April the bootpath leaves the main trail just before the outhouse at the lake outlet and is easy to miss; without it the brush on the slope above is thick with devils club.
Cliff bands lie in the forest above the boulder field, so route-finding matters until you gain the ridge; in April snow then makes the ridge easy walking.
At least a foot of settled snow at the lake makes the lower brush and boulders passable; in late April snow is continuous above roughly 3,400 ft.
From the lake in April, slides and rockfall can be heard and seen coming off the Index gullies across the water; the ridge itself has no avalanche terrain.
In late March snow is thin below about 3,000 ft with a brushy stretch near the start, but above that snowshoes or skis work well.
